title: Interference and distortion
blurb: Explain what causes overload, interference, distorted audio and low power, and the first fix to try for each.

T7B01.why: Louder or closer to the mic means a wider frequency swing. Talking **farther away** brings deviation back down.
T7B01.trap: Talking louder makes it worse. Power level and cooling have nothing to do with deviation.

T7B02.why: A broadcast receiver's front end **can't reject strong signals outside its band**, so your signal gets in anyway.
T7B02.trap: The ham transmitter's audio settings don't affect what a neighbor's receiver does with your carrier.

T7B03.why: Fundamental overload, harmonics and spurious emissions are **all** ways to cause RFI.

T7B04.why: **High SWR** reflects power back, so a solid-state transceiver folds its output power back to protect itself.
T7B04.trap: Low SWR is the good case. Noise figure and linearity affect receiving and distortion, not output power.

T7B05.why: The receiver is the one being overloaded, so put the filter on **its antenna input** and block your signal before it gets in.
T7B05.trap: Filtering your own transmitter won't remove your fundamental. Changing mode doesn't remove it either.

T7B06.why: Start with your own station: make sure it **works properly** and doesn't interfere with your own TV or radio on that channel.
T7B06.trap: Don't shut down and phone the FCC, or add parts like a "harmonic doubler".

T7B07.why: A **band-reject filter** blocks the strong commercial FM signal while leaving your 2 m band alone.
T7B07.trap: A preamp amplifies the interference too. Shielded cable doesn't stop a signal entering at the antenna.

T7B08.why: Work with the neighbor to find the device, explain the FCC rules politely, and make sure your station meets good amateur practice: **all of these**.

T7B09.why: Poorly installed coax connectors leak, so first check that **all TV feed line connectors are installed properly**.
T7B09.trap: Filters and preamps come later. Fix the simple, cheap thing first.

T7B10.why: Off frequency, too loud or too close to the mic, or a poor location can each garble your audio on a repeater: **all of these**.

T7B11.why: A clip-on **ferrite choke** on the mic cable stops your own RF feeding back into the transmitter and distorting your voice.
T7B11.trap: Extra feed line, power cycling or squelch settings don't stop RF on the mic cable.
